ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a left vertical side and a bottom horizontal side, and the lower-left corner is marked with a right angle. The two slanted lines respectively serve as the hypotenuses of two congruent right triangles: one is steeper, going downward from the upper left to connect to the bottom side; the other is gentler, going from the left side down to the right to connect to the far end of the bottom side. The two hypotenuses intersect, and the angle α marked beside the intersection point is the obtuse angle formed by these two hypotenuses. Reasoning: The two triangles are both congruent 40°-50°-90° right triangles. In the triangle corresponding to the steeper hypotenuse, the vertical right-angle side is longer and the horizontal right-angle side is shorter, so this hypotenuse makes 50° with the horizontal bottom side. In the triangle corresponding to the gentler hypotenuse, the vertical right-angle side is shorter and the horizontal right-angle side is longer, so this hypotenuse makes 40° with the horizontal bottom side. Therefore the acute angle between the two hypotenuses is 50° - 40° = 10°. α is the obtuse angle formed by the same two straight lines, and is supplementary to this 10° acute angle, so α = 180° - 10° = 170°.

method.method_draft: Angle-chasing from the common horizontal base: First read the diagram as two right triangles sharing the same left vertical and bottom horizontal directions, with one hypotenuse drawn steeply from the upper left to the bottom base and the other drawn more shallowly from the left side to the far right; the marked angle α is the obtuse angle at the intersection of these two hypotenuses. From the text, use that both triangles are congruent 40°-50°-90° triangles. In the picture, the steeper triangle has the longer leg vertical and shorter leg horizontal, so its hypotenuse makes 50° with the horizontal base; the shallower triangle has the shorter leg vertical and longer leg horizontal, so its hypotenuse makes 40° with the horizontal base. Therefore the acute angle between the two hypotenuses is 50°−40°=10°. Since α is the obtuse supplementary angle formed by the same two lines, α=180°−10°=170°.
